newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers 10 pct of cables firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers 10 pct of cables firm.

text.p: Engineering Industries Company, an Egyptian state holding company, offered investors on Wednesday at least 330,000 shares or 10 percent of its holdings in partly privatised Egyptian Electro Cables.
The public offering is the fourth by the state within a week and is in line with Egypt's privatisation-led economic reform programme.
Engineering Industries Company owns a majority 70 percent of Egyptian Electro Cables while private investors hold 21.7 percent. The employees hold the remaining 8.3 percent.

In a published announcement, the holding company said the offer price would be the stock's closing price on the stock exchange the day before the offer was published. Egyptian Electro Cables ended at 124 pounds ($36.53) on Monday.
Investors must buy at least 5,000 shares. The National Bank of Egypt and brokerage firm al-Rowad are handling the offer, which will open on May 11 and close on May 13.
Incentives for the new shareholders include the dividend per share for the 1996/7 financial year and a place on the firm's board if their holdings warrant.
Dividends for the previous financial year were 9.15 pounds. The year begins on July 1.

Egyptian Electro Cables has had a total 3.3 million shares since it split its shares 10 for one in October 1996. It forecast net profits for 1996/7 to be fractionally higher at 36.60 million pounds, from 36.58 million pounds in 1995/6.
Net sales will be slightly lower at 360.0 million, from 361.1 million in 1995/6.
Egyptian Electro Cables manufactures electric and telephone wires for export and domestic use.
